capabilities.target: Any customer account record, looked up by email or account id

instructions.note: The instruction permits looking up any customer by email or account id with no requirement that the identifier match the requester's own identity.
The agent is told to send routine responses without waiting for a human unless the customer is angry, an unreliable emotional cue rather than a structural check.
The only stated safeguard against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt-level instruction not to share another customer's information, with no structural enforcement behind it.

controls.name: Prompt instruction against cross-customer disclosure
controls.decay_rationale: A more capable model, or one steered by persuasive content embedded in the ticket email, can rationalize exceptions or split the disclosure across steps that each look permitted; compliance with a plain-text prohibition weakens as the model gets better at following long, convincing injected context.

controls.name: MCP server identity verification and definition pinning (recommended)
Raw-action human approval for mismatched sends (recommended)

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: unrestricted cross-customer lookup plus shared-account send discloses other customers' data (TC1/TC4)

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled ticket email requests lookup of an arbitrary account id or email address, exploiting the prompt's grant to look up any customer (prompt.md:3).
Agent calls get_customer with the attacker-supplied identifier using CRM_SVC_TOKEN, which can read every customer record, returning another customer's confidential data.
Agent sends the drafted reply, potentially containing that other customer's data, back to the original requester using MAIL_SVC_TOKEN, a shared service account that can send to any address.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: The model identifier or version string used by support-triage changes, since runtime notes state the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review.

evidence.observation: Instruction allows looking up any customer by email or account id supplied from the inbound ticket, with no requirement that it match the requester.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are both authenticated with static bearer tokens (CRM_SVC_TOKEN, MAIL_SVC_TOKEN) rather than per-user scoped credentials.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.
The agent sends routine responses directly without human approval unless the customer appears angry, so there is no human check before disclosure.
The only safeguard against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction, which is behavioral and dependent on model compliance.

recommendations.action: Restrict crm_mcp lookups to the record matching the verified identity of the ticket requester; reject lookups for identifiers not matching that identity.
Bind the outbound recipient address to the verified requester address stored on the ticket record, rather than letting the agent or a freeform field choose the destination.
Add a raw-action human approval gate for any send where the looked-up account does not match the requester's verified identity.
Alert when outbound email content contains an account identifier that does not match the recipient address on record, using the existing SIEM log as the data source.

findings.title: MCP servers authenticated only by static bearer tokens with no peer identity verification or tool definition pinning (ASI04)

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

forecast.watch_signal: A new entry appears in mcp.json without peer identity verification or pinned tool definitions.

evidence.observation: Both MCP server entries authenticate via a static bearer token header with no indication of mutual TLS or signed server identity.
No mention of tool definition pinning or hashing for crm_mcp or mail_mcp, leaving them open to rug-pull style redefinition or, if the endpoint were impersonated, to bearer token capture.

recommendations.action: Require mutual TLS or signed server identity verification for crm_mcp and mail_mcp connections instead of relying on a bearer token alone.
Pin or hash tool definitions for crm_mcp and mail_mcp and verify the hash before each session to detect rug-pull changes.

stride_coverage.rationale: The design does not describe how the agent authenticates itself to users or downstream systems beyond the MCP server bearer tokens, so agent identity spoofing risk is not assessed.
The agent has no configure capability and cannot modify its own prompt or config; no capability in the design allows tampering with agent configuration.
The agent processes tickets individually with no spend capability or recursive execution; the design describes no unbounded loop or self-spawning behavior that could cause resource exhaustion.
The design does not state whether sender authentication such as SPF or DKIM, or ticket system identity verification, is applied to inbound email, so attribution strength is not assessed.

Transport integrity of the inbound mail channel is outside this design's scope; the risk assessed is the content's untrusted origin, covered under information_disclosure for this flow, not in-transit tampering.
The design does not state whether inbound ticket volume is rate limited, so flood-induced denial of service risk is not assessed.
Transit integrity of outbound mail to the mail server is not in scope; the risk assessed is the recipient and content selected by the agent, covered in finding.1.
The design does not state whether outbound send volume or rate is capped, so mail-based denial of service or reputation risk is not assessed.
The design does not state whether SIEM log entries are write-once or tamper-evident, so log integrity is not assessed.
The design does not state access controls on the SIEM log itself, so secondary disclosure risk via log access is not assessed.
Log storage capacity is an operational SIEM concern outside this agent's design and not described as a function of agent behavior.
The agent's only capability on this store is read (cap.crm_read); no write or delete capability is declared, so tampering via the agent is not applicable.
Read-only access via a single lookup per ticket does not create a resource exhaustion path absent a bulk query capability, which is not declared.
The design does not state whether crm_mcp logs individual query requests with caller identity, so repudiation risk for read actions is not assessed.
The design does not state rate limiting or availability safeguards on the crm_mcp server itself.
The design does not state whether mail_mcp enforces a send rate limit, so denial of service or spam-reputation risk is not assessed.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted ticket email can direct a lookup of any customer's confidential record and trigger an irreversible, externally-egressing send via a shared service account, with the autonomy modifier applied because no step or runtime limit is declared. The only present control on that path is a behavioral prompt instruction, which earns one tier of credit under rubric section 5 step 4, giving a residual of high; the structural fixes that would sever or narrow the path (identity-bound reads, recipient binding, a raw-action approval gate) are recommended but not yet implemented. Forecast returns to critical because the design states the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, and that upgrade is exactly the trigger that defeats a dependent, behavioral control. A second, independent property finding on unverified MCP server identity and unpinned tool definitions adds a high-rated supply-chain exposure that does not depend on the first finding's controls.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, server-side authorization logic, or agent card was provided beyond mcp.json; whether crm_mcp or mail_mcp enforce any scoping beyond the bearer token is inferred as absent, which the report flags as not_assessed rather than scored with high confidence.
No IaC or source code was provided; autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not stated and were assumed null per the rubric's autonomy modifier rule.
